THE OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY, HEALTH AND WORKING  
CONDITIONS CODE, 2020  
INTRODUCTION  
§
§
The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code “the Code” is a law  
related to labour reforms.  
It is a Code to consolidate and amend the laws regulating the occupational safety,  
health and working conditions of the persons employed in an establishment.  
§
Section 3 of the Code lays don that it shall not apply to the offices of the:  
ü Central Government,  
ü State Government and  
ü any ship of war of any nationality  
•
the Code shall apply in case of:  
o contract labour employed through contractor in the offices of the  
Central Government or of the State Government, where, the Central  
Government or, as the case may be, the State Government is the  
principal employer.

§
Section 2 (b) "adult" means a person who has completed his eighteenth year of age.  
Section 2 (c) "agent" when used in relation to a mine, means every person, whether

Section 2 (m) "contract labour" means a worker is considered employed in or in  
connection with the work of an establishment when hired through a contractor, regardless  
of the principal employer's kowledge. This definition includes inter-State migrant workers.  
However, it excludes workers regularly employed by the contractor for any activity of their  
establishment, where their employment follows mutually agreed-upon standards,  
including engagement on a permanent basis. These workers receive periodic increments  
in pay, social security coverage, and other welfare benefits as per the prevailing laws.  
Notably, part-time employees are not included in this exclusion.

Section 2 (n) "contractor", in relation to an establishment, means a person, who— (i)  
undertakes to produce a given result for the establishment, other than a mere supply of

§
Section 2 (o) "controlled industry" means any industry the control of which by the  
Central Government has been declared under any Central Act in the public interest.  
Section 2 (p) "core activity of an establishment" means an essential or necessary  
activity in an establishment refers to any function for which the establishment is  
established. This includes activities that are vital or required for the main activity. However,  
certain activities are not considered essential or necessary if the establishment is not  
primarily set up for them. These non-essential activities include: (a) Sanitation works, such  
as sweeping, cleaning, dusting, and waste collection and disposal, (b) Watch and ward  
services, including security services, (c) Canteen and catering services, (d) Loading and  
unloading operations, (e) Running hospitals, educational and training institutions, guest  
houses, clubs, etc., if they serve as support services, (f) Courier services that function as  
support services, (g) Civil and other constructional works, including maintenance, (h)  
Gardening and maintenance of lawns and similar activities, (i) Housekeeping and laundry  
services, if they are support services, (j) Transport services, including ambulance services,  
(j) Any activity of intermittent nature, even if it constitutes a core activity of the  
establishment.

§
Section 2 (q) "day" means a period of twenty-four hours beginning at mid-night.  
Section 2 (s) "dock work" means any work in or within the vicinity of any port in connection  
with, or required for, or incidental to, the loading, unloading, movement or storage of

Section 2 (t) "employee" means an individual (excluding an apprentice under the

as an employee by the appropriate Government, excluding members of the Armed Forces  
of the Union. Employee in a Mine is someone who works in various capacities, including

Loading minerals for dispatch, Office work within the mine, Welfare, health, sanitary, or

Section 2 (v) "establishment" means (i) a place where any industry, trade, business,  
manufacturing or occupation is carried on in which ten or more workers are employed; or  
(ii) motor transport undertaking, newspaper establishment, audio-video production,  
building and other construction work or plantation, in which ten or more workers are

§
Section 2 (w) "factory" means any premises including the precincts thereof— (i) whereon  
twenty or more workers are working, or were working on any day of the preceding twelve  
months, and in any part of which a manufacturing process is being carried on with the aid  
of power, or is ordinarily so carried on; or (ii) whereon forty or more workers are working,  
or were working on any day of the preceding twelve months, and in any part of which a

in that State till it is amended by the competent Legislature.

Section 2 (zs) "occupier" of a factory means the person who has ultimate control over

REGISTRATION OF CERTAIN ESTABLISHMENTS SECTION 3  
§
§
§
§
§
§
Employers of establishments that come into existence after the commencement of the  
Code must submit an electronic application for registration within 60 days. Late  
applications are subject to prescribed late fees.  
Upon receiving the registration application, the registering officer must register the  
establishment and issue an electronic certificate of registration within the specified  
time frame and conditions set by the Central Government.  
If the registering officer fails to register the establishment within the prescribed period,  
the establishment is automatically deemed registered, and the electronic certificate  
will be auto-generated.  
Employers must notify the registering officer of any changes in ownership,  
management, or details of the establishment within 30 days. The registration certificate  
will be amended accordingly.  
If an establishment closes, the employer must inform the registering officer and  
certify the payment of all worker dues within 30 days. The officer must remove the  
establishment from the register and cancel the certificate within 60 days.  
If registration is obtained by misrepresentation or fraud, the employer may face  
prosecution or the registering officer may revoke the registration, after providing the  
employer an opportunity to be heard.  
§
§
Employers without proper registration or who fail to appeal cancellation or  
revocation cannot employ workers in the establishment.  
An establishment already registered under other relevant laws will be considered  
registered under the new Occupational Safety, Health, and Working Conditions Code  
upon submitting registration details to the registering officer.  
APPEAL SECTION 4  
6
THE OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY, HEALTH AND WORKING  
CONDITIONS CODE, 2020  
§
Any person aggrieved by an order under section 3 may file an appeal within 30 days  
of being informed about the decision.  
§
§
The appeal will be handled by an appellate officer appointed by the government.  
If the appellate officer is satisfied, they may accept an appeal even if it is filed after the  
30-day period.  
§
Upon receiving the appeal, the appellate officer must give the appellant an opportunity to  
be heard and dispose of the appeal within 30 days from the date of receipt.  
NOTICE BY EMPLOYER OF COMMENCEMENT AND CESSATION OF OPERATION  
SECTION 5  
§
Before starting any business, trade, or construction work in a factory, mine, or other  
covered establishments, the employer must notify the appropriate authority with  
details about the nature of the work.  
§
§
The employer must also inform the authority when the operation ceases.  
The notice or intimation must be given electronically.  
DUTIES OF EMPLOYER AND EMPLOYEES, ETC. SECTION 6  
§
Every employer shall:  
ü ensure workplace is free from hazards causing injury or occupational disease.  
ü comply with occupational safety and health standards, rules, and regulations under  
this Code.  
ü provide free annual health exams or tests as prescribed for specific employees or  
establishments.  
ü maintain a safe and healthy working environment, as far as reasonably practicable.  
ü ensure proper disposal of hazardous, toxic, and e-waste.  
ü issue appointment letters to employees, if not already done, within three months  
of the Code's commencement.  
ü ensure no charges are levied on employees for maintaining safety and health,  
including medical examinations.  
ü ensure the safety and health of employees, workers, and others on work premises,  
with or without employer knowledge.  
§
The duties of an employer shall particularly in respect of factory, mines, dock,  
building or other construction work or plantation include:  
ü provide and maintain safe plant and work systems that pose no health risks.  
ü ensure safety and health during the use, handling, storage, and transport of articles  
and substances.  
ü provide necessary information, instruction, training, and supervision to ensure  
employee health and safety.  
ü maintain workplaces in a safe condition, with safe access and egress.  
ü ensure a safe working environment that promotes employee welfare and is free  
from health risks.  
DUTIES OF DESIGNERS, MANUFACTURERS, IMPORTERS OR SUPPLIERS SECTION 8  
7
THE OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY, HEALTH AND WORKING  
CONDITIONS CODE, 2020  
§
Every person who designs, manufactures, imports or supplies any article for use in  
any establishment shall:  
ü ensure that the article is designed and constructed in a way that is safe and poses  
no risk to workers' health when used correctly, as far as reasonably practicable.  
ü carry out or arrange for necessary tests and examinations to ensure the article’s  
safety.  
ü provide sufficient information on how the article should be used safely, including  
details on design, testing, and necessary safety conditions for workers.  
ü for imported articles, ensure they meet the same safety standards as those made  
in India. If the standards in the country of origin are higher, the article must meet  
those higher standards. If no specific standards exist in India, the article must  
comply with the standards from the country of origin.  
§
The designer, manufacturer, importer, or supplier must also:  
ü comply with any additional duties specified by the Central Government, in  
consultation with the National Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board  
ü conduct necessary research to identify and eliminate or minimize health and  
safety risks related to the article or substance being designed or manufactured for  
use in a factory.  
§
§
Responsibilities apply only to activities conducted in the course of business and  
matters under the person’s control.  
Every person who:  
ü erects or installs an article in a factory must ensure it does not pose a risk to health  
or safety when used by workers.  
ü manufactures, imports, or supplies a substance for use in a factory must ensure  
the substance is not unsafe, conduct necessary tests, and ensure safety  
information is available in the factory.  
ü undertakes the manufacture of a substance for use in a factory must conduct  
research to identify and reduce health and safety risks from the substance's  
manufacture.  
§
Articles and substances must not be used in the factory without considering any  
safety information or advice provided by the designer, manufacturer, importer, or  
supplier.  
§
§
"Article" shall include plant and machinery;  
"Substance" means any natural or artificial substance whether in a solid or liquid form or in the form of a gas or vapour;  
and  
§
"Substance for use in any factory" means such substance, whether or not intended for use by persons working in a  
factory.  
DUTIES OF ARCHITECT, PROJECT ENGINEER AND DESIGNER SECTION 9  
§
Architects, project engineers, and designers are responsible for ensuring worker safety  
and health during the planning stage of a construction project.  
8
THE OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY, HEALTH AND WORKING  
CONDITIONS CODE, 2020  
§
§
§
They must identify and address potential risks, including hazards related to structures,  
processes, and materials used in the project.  
The design must avoid unsafe practices that could compromise the health or safety of  
workers during construction, operation, or execution.  
Professionals must also consider safety measures for the ongoing maintenance and  
upkeep of the building or structure, particularly for hazards notified by the appropriate  
government.  
NOTICE OF CERTAIN ACCIDENT SECTION 10  
§
Serious accidents in establishments (death, significant injury, or inability to work for  
48+ hours) must be reported to relevant authorities by:  
ü Employer, owner, agent, or manager (for mines).  
ü Employer or manager (for factories or dock work).  
ü Employer (for plantations, construction, or other establishments).  
Reporting must follow the manner and timeline specified by the appropriate  
government.  
§
§
For accidents causing death in plantations, construction, or other establishments:  
ü Inquiry must be conducted within two months of notice submission.  
ü If no authority is designated, the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator ensures the  
Inspector-cum-Facilitator conducts the inquiry.  
ü Inquiry investigates accident circumstances and collects relevant information.  
DUTIES OF EMPLOYEES SECTION 13  
§
Employee shall:  
ü Take reasonable care of their own health and safety as well as that of others who  
may be affected by their actions or inactions at the workplace.  
ü Comply with safety and health requirements outlined in the applicable standards.  
ü Cooperate with their employer to help meet statutory obligations under this Code.  
ü Promptly report any unsafe or unhealthy situation to their employer, health and  
safety representative, or designated workplace official, as applicable.  
ü Not willfully interfere with, misuse, or neglect any equipment or facilities provided  
for workplace health, safety, and welfare.  
ü Avoid willful actions or omissions that could endanger themselves or others  
without reasonable cause.  
ü Perform any additional duties prescribed by the appropriate Government.  
RIGHTS OF EMPLOYEE SECTION 14  
§
§
Employees have the right to ask their employer for information about their health and  
safety at work.  
Employees can report concerns about inadequate safety measures or health risks  
to their employer or through a Safety Committee, if available.  
9
THE OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY, HEALTH AND WORKING  
CONDITIONS CODE, 2020  
§
§
If unresolved, employees can approach the Inspector-cum-Facilitator, a designated  
authority for addressing workplace safety issues.  
If an employee reasonably believes there is an imminent risk of serious injury, death,  
or danger to health, they can notify their employer directly or through a Safety  
Committee member and simultaneously inform the Inspector-cum-Facilitator.  
Employers or employees must take immediate action if the concern about imminent  
danger is valid and report the action taken to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator.  
If the employer disagrees with the employee's concern about imminent danger,  
they must still refer the matter to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator without delay.  
§
§
NATIONAL OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH ADVISORY BOARD SECTION 16  
§
The Central Government will establish the National Occupational Safety and Health  
Advisory Board (NOSHAB) to perform functions under this Code and provide advice on:  
ü Standards, rules, and regulations under the Code.  
ü Implementation of the Code and related regulations.  
ü Policy and program issues regarding occupational safety and health.  
ü Any other matters referred by the Central Government.  
The Central Government may constitute technical committees or advisory committees to  
assist the NOSHAB in discharge of its function.  
§
§
NOSHAB shall consist of:  
ü Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Employment (Chairperson ex officio).  
ü Director General, Factory Advice Service and Labour Institutes, Mumbai (Member  
ex officio).  
ü Director General, Mines Safety, Dhanbad (Member ex officio).  
ü Chief Controller of Explosives, Nagpur (Member ex officio).  
ü Chairman, Central Pollution Control Board, New Delhi (Member ex officio).  
ü Chief Labour Commissioner (Central), New Delhi (Member ex officio).  
ü Principal Secretaries of Labour from four States (by rotation, 3-year tenure).  
ü Director General, Employee's State Insurance Corporation, New Delhi (Member  
ex officio).  
ü Director General, Health Services, New Delhi (Member ex officio).  
ü Five representatives of employers (3-year tenure).  
ü Five representatives of employees (3-year tenure).  
ü One representative of a professional body involved in standards, rules, or policy-  
making (3-year tenure).  
ü Five eminent persons or representatives from reputed research institutions in  
occupational safety and health (3-year tenure).  
ü Special invitees from State or Union Territory Governments for specific inputs on  
matters related to predominant industries or sectors.  
ü Joint Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Employment (Member Secretary ex officio).  
STATE OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH ADVISORY BOARD SECTION 17  
10  
THE OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY, HEALTH AND WORKING  
CONDITIONS CODE, 2020  
§
The State Government shall establish the State Occupational Safety and Health  
Advisory Board (SOSHAB) to advise on matters related to the administration of the  
Code.  
§
The State Government can form technical or advisory committees under SOSHAB,  
including site appraisal committees, to assist in responsibilities specific to their  
jurisdictions.  
OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH STANDARDS SECTION 18  
§
The Central Government sets occupational safety and health standards for  
workplaces like factories, mines, dock work, beedi and cigar production, construction  
sites, and similar environments.  
§
§
Standards address physical, chemical, biological, and other hazards to prevent health  
impairment or loss of functional capacity during employees' working lives.  
Norms include:  
ü Identifying hazards and symptoms for employees and users exposed to them.  
ü Ensuring proper treatment, safe usage conditions, and exposure precautions.  
ü Monitoring and measuring employees' exposure to hazards.  
ü Providing employer-funded medical exams and tests for exposed employees.  
ü Conducting hazard evaluation procedures like safety audits and hazard analyses.  
Medical examinations for detecting and reporting occupational diseases are  
extended to employees even after employment if the disease arises from their work.  
The Central Government determines necessary safety and health measures based on  
designated authority reports and workplace-specific conditions.  
Standards cover aspects listed in the Second Schedule to the Code.  
The Central Government can amend the Second Schedule after a minimum of 45  
days' notice, following recommendations from NOSHAB.  
§
§
§
§
SAFETY AND OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH SURVEYS SECTION 20  
§
During working hours or as necessary, authorized authorities may conduct surveys in  
factories, mines, or other establishments. Authorities include:  
ü Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator in the case of factory or mine, or  
ü Director General of Factory Advice Service and Labour Institute in the case of  
factory; or  
ü the Director General of Mines Safety in the case of mine; or  
ü the Director General of Health Services in the case of factory or mine; or  
ü such other officer as may be authorised by the appropriate Government in the case  
of any other establishment or class of establishments,  
§
§
§
Employers will receive prior written notice before the survey is conducted and must  
provide facilities for testing machinery, collecting samples, and gathering relevant data.  
Workers may be required to undergo medical examinations and provide relevant  
information during surveys.  
Time spent by workers on such activities will be treated as working hours for wage  
and overtime calculations.
